title: Staged rollout: NVIDIA driver memory leak causing soft failures
content:
Executive summary:

During a controlled, region-by-region staged rollout of the weight-apply optimization (runtime PR #2140) on 2024-09-18 we observed a class of intermittent 'soft' failures in the Hosted API in eu-west-1 and us-central-1. Symptoms were elevated 5xx rates from a subset of GPU-backed pods without full process crashes or kernel panics. Affected requests experienced long tail latency and occasional model decode failures that resolved after request retry or pod recycle.

Impact:
- Duration: ~09:15–14:40 UTC on 2024-09-18 (mitigation began at 13:05 UTC).
- Scope: ~3% of production generative requests in eu-west-1 and ~1.2% in us-central-1 during the rollout window.
- User-visible: Increased error surface (500s) and p95/p99 latency spikes for affected customers; no data loss, no long-term model regressions observed.
- Business: Small subset of interactive sessions experienced degraded UX and a few customer SLAs were narrowly missed.

Detection and monitoring signals that alerted us:
- Canary dashboards: sudden rise in canary endpoint p99 latency for the new runtime variant at 09:20 UTC.
- SRE alerts: pod-level GPU memory pressure metric (nvidia_smi_memory_used_bytes) showed a slow upward drift across affected pods, not correlated with request rate.
- Observability traces: increased tail latencies on function calls that perform KV cache and weight apply; stack traces pointed to cublas/cuDNN calls followed by extended allocation churn.
- Node-level logs: kernel logs did not show OOM kills; driver logs (nvidia-container-toolkit + dmesg) contained repeated lines indicating driver-side allocation failures with recovery: "NVRM: GPU: X; nv_alloc failed, reclaiming asynchronously".

Timeline (high level):
- 09:00 UTC: staged rollout begins in canary ring (10% of capacity) with new weight-apply kernel selection heuristics enabled.
- 09:20 UTC: canary p99 latency increases; initial assumption: batching config interaction; rollout paused at 09:30 UTC.
- 10:05 UTC: SRE investigates; memory-used metrics show upward trend even at low QPS.
- 11:00 UTC: Additional tests reproduce increasing GPU memory fragmentation when the new code path (different pinned allocation pattern) is exercised repeatedly.
- 12:15 UTC: mitigation experiment — revert kernel selection to previous heuristics on a small set of pods; memory trend stabilizes on reverted pods.
- 13:05 UTC: global rollback of staged rollout (stop rollout + roll pods back to previous runtime) initiated.
- 14:40 UTC: metrics returned to baseline; incident declared mitigated.

Root cause hypothesis (what we believe happened):
- The new weight-apply optimization changed the allocation pattern for GPU memory (more small pinned host->device transfers and a different CUDA allocation API path).
- On specific NVIDIA driver microversions present in eu-west-1 and us-central-1, this allocation churn triggered a driver-side memory fragmentation/leak behavior where allocations were not reclaimed efficiently, leading to slow GPU memory growth inside the driver state (observed as "used" increase via nvidia-smi), but without user-space process OOM.
- The driver attempted soft recovery (reclaim paths) which introduced latency and intermittent allocation failures observed as transient 5xx responses.
- The behavior only surfaced under continuous weight apply paths (i.e., during model reloads/weight swaps or high micro-burst decode operations) — explaining the staged rollout correlation and why a subset of pods were affected.

Evidence collected:
- Heap/alloc traces from a repro harness showing repeated pinned allocations with increasing resident set in driver logs.
- Repro on a node with the same driver version using a synthetic workload exercising the new code path showing identical memory growth.
- Reverting to previous kernel selection stops the growth consistently.
- Driver vendor (NVIDIA) internal logs and early triage indicate known corner-case in driver v535.xx when using a particular allocation/release pattern.

Immediate mitigation performed:
1) Pause rollout at 09:30 UTC once canary p99 elevated.
2) Scoped rollback testing at 12:15 UTC by reverting runtime heuristics on small group; validated stability.
3) Full rollback + redeploy to prior runtime variant at 13:05 UTC.
4) Proactive pod recycle for nodes with persistent elevated driver memory.
5) Notified affected customers and internal stakeholders.

Short-term fixes (next 7 days):
- Pin staged rollout in eu-west-1 and us-central-1 to the previous runtime variant until driver patch is available.
- Add an SLO-based gating rule to the rollout controller: if node-driver memory_used increases > 10% over baseline for 15m without QPS increase, automatically abort rollout and trigger pod-level revert.
- Extend canary runtime tests to include synthetic allocation churn workloads that mimic weight-apply patterns.
- Open ticket with NVIDIA (refer to linked JIRA) and provide collection of driver logs and repro harness.

Long-term actions (owner assigned):
- eng/serving-runtime: modify allocation path to use allocation pooling (OWNER: Aisha Kapoor; ETA: 2024-10-15) — reduces churn and reliance on driver reclaim heuristics.
- infra/SRE: implement driver-version-aware rollout policies that avoid known-bad driver microversions (OWNER: Ethan Walker; ETA: 2024-10-01).
- QA: add a sustained memory-leak fuzz test to CI that runs for 6 hours on a small GPU node with the allocation pattern (OWNER: Sofia Ramirez; ETA: 2024-11-01).
- Product: update rollout playbook to include driver-level metrics as first-class gating criteria (OWNER: Marcus Liu; ETA: 2024-09-30).

Runbook / playbook additions (draft):
- Pre-rollout checks: verify driver versions in target region; ensure none match blacklisted microversions.
- During rollout: monitor nvidia_smi_memory_used_bytes and driver reclaim error counters; set a soft abort threshold.
- Recovery steps: if soft failures detected, revert kernel selection heuristics -> wait 20m -> if stable, continue with slower ramp; else roll back completely.
- Escalation: open vendor support ticket with driver logs attached; include reproducible harness steps.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact root cause inside driver reclaim path — driver vendor feedback pending.
- Why certain hardware SKUs in the same region were unaffected; need node inventory correlation.
- Whether other future allocation changes could re-trigger similar behavior; need to harden allocation interface.

Appendix (selected logs / snippets):
- Driver log excerpt (anonymized):
  [2024-09-18T09:22:41Z] NVRM: GPU 0: nv_alloc: failed to allocate 0x4000000 bytes; reclaiming
  [2024-09-18T09:22:42Z] NVRM: GPU 0: reclaim attempted, success=false, in_flight=3
  [2024-09-18T09:23:01Z] containerd: exec: request id=... status=500: allocation failure on device GPU 0

- Observability snippet: canary-runtime-variant p99 latency: baseline 220ms -> observed 1.2s at peak.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally focused on the SRE/infra aspects; for model-level impacts and customer comms, see parallel product postmortem (linked in JIRA-3497).
- Please review runbook wording — need explicit thresholds for automatic abort behavior.
- If you can reproduce on a lab node with driver v535.86, add logs to JIRA-3482.

Actions logged (short):
- JIRA-3482: Driver memleak repro + vendor ticket (created 2024-09-18).
- JIRA-3497: Rollout rollback and customer notification (created 2024-09-18).

Prepared by: Marcus Liu (SRE)
Reviewed by: Aisha Kapoor, Sofia Ramirez

Status: in_review — please add comments inline and assign owners for long-term items.
